title: Stephen
html_source:
There’s not much more jaw dropping than the efficiency of beauty and Gilbert sure packs it in here in his chapter on Scylla and Charybdis.

‘Such are a few of the numerous cross-correspondences and allusions, literary, legendary, or personal to Stephan Dedalus, which abound in this episode, many-headed and elusive as the monster Scylla herself. It remains to consider the general import of this quasi-Platonic dialogue, in which Stephen plays the role of a Socrates, and of the curious conclusion to which the young Symposiarch leads his reluctant elders along a dialectic tightrope. Briefly, this conclusion is that in the play of Hamlet the author identifies himself rather with hamlet pere than with Hamlet fils, and that, therefore, thw groundling in his opinion of the personality of Shakespeare is clean abused’
http://www.amazon.co.uk/James-Joyces-Ulysses-Stuart-Gilbert/dp/B005H3GYJG/ref=sr_1_12?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1405010014&sr=1-12&keywords=gilbert+james+joyce+ulysses

I got a 1963 Gilbert from Amazon, O consumer Artificer, shilling signs, frictionless gleam of the cover and nostril flaring sting of the glue !
